stability: surface_version covers ONLY what an outside caller can say: the set of loops, the set
of modes, and each command's required and optional flags. That is the promise, and it
is pinned in surface.lock — --selftest recomputes it and goes red on any drift, so the
promise cannot move by accident. Changing it means bumping surface_version and running
`loopctl.sh surface-relock`, which refuses to relock while the version is unchanged.
Everything else is internal and free to iterate without touching that promise: which
file implements a command (target), what it writes, how it is invoked, and the whole
of loopctl.sh's dispatch. Move a target, rewrite an entry point, change its private
flags -- the surface digest does not move, and external callers keep working.
The two are separately visible on purpose. Internal drift shows up in each loop's own
proof receipt; surface drift shows up here. Collapsing them into one number would make
ordinary internal iteration indistinguishable from a broken promise.
purpose: The only surface an outside caller is meant to touch. Each loop has one entry point,
and reaching past this file into the entry point's own flags -- or worse, editing the
entry point to make a call site work -- is the jitter this exists to stop.
This file is the SURFACE and is machine-readable on purpose: `loopctl.sh contract`
prints it with a sha256, so a changed surface is a visible event rather than a quiet
one. How each target is invoked is wiring and lives in loopctl.sh; the two are held
together by --selftest, which fails if either side gains an entry the other lacks.
Exit codes are passed through from the target verbatim, never re-mapped:
0 ok - 2 the loop's own check failed - 64 usage, contract violation, or a FATAL
(absent tool, absent input) from the target itself.

modes.run: execute the loop's real entry point
modes.prove: traverse it and write a proof receipt under data/proof-workflow/
modes.test: run the control group: execute the entry point in isolation and compare what it really touches against the proof
modes.lock: rebuild the manifest of what a traversal is made of, from the proof receipts
modes.trailer: print the lineage trailer this commit should carry (empty when no workflow file is staged)
modes.replay: check a commit or tag out into a disposable worktree and run THAT version's CLI
modes.serve: run the stateless MCP server on stdio, one disposable worktree per call
modes.build: build the OCI image the container layer serves from

arg_groups.packet: --packet + --output — hand it a packet you already have
arg_groups.source: --source + --task [+ --kind, --packet-id, --output] — hand it a document or a repo and let the CLI build the packet

input.--packet: path to an input packet JSON, schema perfect-seed-input-packet; validated by src/cli.ts `validate` before anything runs. Must carry packet_id and source_refs; refs_status must be declared|sentinel|resolved, and stale is refused (exit 2)
input.--source: a document or a directory to ingest instead of writing a packet by hand. .md/.txt go in as they are; .html/.htm and .pdf are extracted first; a directory becomes --kind repo. Any other format is refused rather than decoded — a .docx read as utf-8 yields lines that look exactly like evidence and are noise. Extraction records the original path and sha256, the extractor argv and version, and the extracted sha256 in provenance.json next to the packet, so an evidence line pointing at extracted.txt stays resolvable back to the original
input.--kind: dr (default) | gcr | grill-me | repo — the SEMANTIC kind, orthogonal to the file format, which is detected from the extension
input.--task: required with --source: the one-line task the seed repo is being built to answer
input.--packet-id: override the id derived from the source's name
input.--output: ABSOLUTE path for the seed repo to be materialized at. It must NOT already exist — cli.ts:23 refuses an existing path, so every run needs a fresh one. This is the single most common caller mistake and it fails at step one, not halfway

output: packets/outbox/route-result.<packet_id>.json — schema perfect-seed-route-result@1.0.0, carrying four separate stage exits (build, fast_quality, operator, validator) and next_edge=human_required_before_seed_admit
data/wiki-update/request-<packet_id>.json — schema bettor-arena-wiki-update-request@1.0.0; this is the openwiki loop's input, which is how the two loops are chained
io.exit: 0 all four stages green · 2 a stage failed (the route-result still lands, carrying which one) · 64 usage
io.note: outside a git repo the wiki-update request is a NAMED skip rather than a failure, so the factory stays relocatable

input.--request: path to a wiki-update request JSON, schema bettor-arena-wiki-update-request@1.0.0 — normally the one `micro run` just produced. It carries three separate context lanes: fixed (pointers to the official prompt assets, never copied text), iteration (the deterministic delta from the last documented gitHead), emergent (a pointer to openwiki/quickstart.md#backlog). Every field is checked before any work: a missing one is exit 2 by name, and delta_status must be computed|no-last-update|unresolvable-last-head

output: data/wiki-update/receipt-<packet_id>.json — per-stage record back-linking request_id; refuses to overwrite without --force-receipt

arg_groups.target: --target NAME — a harvest declared in notebooklm/registry.json, which carries its own notebook title, source pick and follow decision

opt_in.--follow: hop 2: really open a docs.google document linked from inside the harvested sheet, BY DRIVE FILE ID over the signed-in session. It is the only WRITING path here, and it writes to a scratch notebook it creates and deletes again from `finally` — never to the notebook being harvested. Without it the run is read-only. It goes through notebooklm/drive_fetch.py under the CLI's own interpreter because the CLI has no authenticated Drive path and its `source add <url>` is an ANONYMOUS fetch: measured, every document linked from this sheet answers HTTP 401 to an anonymous request (a nonexistent id answers 404, which is how gated was told apart from absent) and the CLI returned FAILED_PRECONDITION for all of them
opt_in.--dry-run: run every READ stage for real (auth, notebook resolution, registry pin check, source pick) and stop before the first fetch, printing the argv of every call point including the ones --follow would make

input.--target: an entry in notebooklm/registry.json — this repo's interaction data for notebooklm-py. Exactly one of --target and --notebook-title must be given: both would silently pick a winner, neither would reach the account with no subject (exit 64 either way)
input.--notebook-title: the EXACT title of the notebook to harvest. A title is not an id: two notebooks sharing one is exit 2 by name, never a silent pick. When the registry pins that title, the pin is still cross-checked against the live account and a disagreement is exit 2
input.--source-title: harvest this exact Doc/Sheet title instead of the default pick. The default is the AI-related ready sources, spreadsheets first, then by title — spreadsheets first because only a sheet plausibly carries the links hop 2 follows
input.--registry: an alternative registry file; default notebooklm/registry.json
input.--out: directory for this run's artifacts; default data/notebooklm/<utc>
input.--timeout: seconds to wait for the followed document to index (default 600)

output: <out>/module.json — schema bettor-arena-notebooklm-module@1.0.0: the notebook and source it resolved, every candidate it saw, the doc URLs found, and hop 2's state. Carries sha256 and counts, never document text
<out>/hop1.txt — the harvested source's indexed text (not written by --dry-run)
